body: Distilled from ~30 blow-ups (Satyam, DHFL, IL&FS, Yes Bank, Cox & Kings, Ricoh, Zee, ADAG, Future, Enron, WorldCom, Wirecard, Valeant, GE...). Score each; 3+ hits = do not own without a variant view. CASH: (1) cumulative CFO / cumulative PAT < 0.7 over 5 years; (2) FCF negative for 3+ years while reporting profits; (3) interest income / average cash far below market rates (Satyam fake cash); (4) cash held by third parties/trustees or 'restricted' (Wirecard). WORKING CAPITAL: (5) receivable days or inventory days rising faster than sales for 2+ years (Ricoh, PC Jeweller); (6) working-capital sign contradicts business model (Cox & Kings). CAPITALISATION: (7) capex/sales or capitalised R&D/interest rising vs peers; CWIP aging (WorldCom). RELATED PARTIES: (8) loans/advances/investments to promoter entities, 'general purpose corporate loans' (RHFL); related-party acquisitions (Maytas). GOVERNANCE: (9) auditor resignation, qualified opinion, delayed results (Byju's, Ricoh); (10) independent-director or CFO exits; (11) promoter pledge >25% or rising, falling promoter stake (Zee, Satyam); (12) frequent restructurings/demergers/name changes. BALANCE SHEET: (13) net debt/EBITDA >4x or interest cover <2x outside utilities (IL&FS); (14) short-term funding of long assets. MARKET: (15) rating downgrades/CP-spread spikes; (16) credible short-seller report; (17) insider selling into strength; (18) regulator action on management (Yes Bank). Composite screens: Beneish M > -1.78, Altman Z < 1.81, Piotroski F <= 3 (see separate insights).

data.rule: 3+ flags = no position without variant perception; any of auditor exit, related-party diversion, fake-cash signal = disqualifier

title: Forensic red-flag checklist (pre-blowup signals)

body: Cases: ASML (only EUV supplier; ~22x 2012-24), TSMC (leading-edge foundry; ADR ~24x to $363 and a $2tn market cap by 2026), Nvidia (AI compute; see case_study:nvidia). Pattern: the moat is built in public over 5-10 years of technical risk. Early signals: customers paying to secure supply (Intel/TSMC/Samsung €3.85bn for 23% of ASML in 2012; hyperscalers pre-paying for capacity), competitors publicly slipping (Intel 10nm delays 2016-20, GlobalFoundries exiting 7nm 2018), and rising gross margin despite heavy capex/depreciation. Why under-priced: cyclicality (each still fell -55-60% in 2022), concentration on few customers, and geopolitics (TSMC's Taiwan discount; ASML's China export limits). Notable misses: the strategic investors sold early (TSMC sold its ASML stake in 2015; Intel and Samsung trimmed from 2016), and Berkshire reportedly bought and quickly sold TSMC in 2022 on geopolitical risk [unverified]. Lesson: monopolies at technological chokepoints can be owned through cycles, but size them so the tail risk (export bans, Taiwan) is survivable; buy in the cyclical drawdowns, not at AI-peak multiples.

data.signal: customer co-investment; rival process slips; GM up with capex

title: Chokepoint monopolies: customers co-invest, the market under-prices for years
